problem: The notation drops the vector: 'p=0.9 gives ρ=diag(0.9,0.1)'. Earlier p is defined as the vector p=(p₀,p₁), and elsewhere p is also used as a single binary probability. A student may read p=0.9 as a number, not a distribution.
fix: Write it as: p=(0.9,0.1) gives ρ=diag(0.9,0.1).

problem: Writing S(|+⟩)=0 is shorthand: S is defined on a density matrix ρ, not on a ket. A student may think entropy can be taken of |ψ⟩ directly and be confused about which object the formula applies to.
fix: Write S(|+⟩⟨+|)=0, and note that S of a ket always means S of its density matrix |ψ⟩⟨ψ|.

problem: 'Quantum systems have a similar quantity for bipartite states' is too vague; the quantity is not named, so the reader cannot connect it to the classical I(X:Y) beside it.
fix: Say explicitly: the quantum mutual information of a bipartite state ρ_AB is I(A:B)=S(ρ_A)+S(ρ_B)−S(ρ_AB), which reduces to H(X)+H(Y)−H(X,Y) when ρ_AB is diagonal in a product basis.
